University of Helsinki tuition fee waivers (master's) and Aalto University scholarships for fee-paying non-EU/EEA students.

items.description: Monthly study grant for higher education students. EU/EEA, Swiss and UK degree students who moved to Finland to study usually do NOT qualify, unless they work in Finland, have permanent residence under EU law, have a working EU family member in Finland, or came for another reason and live in Finland permanently. Exchange students never qualify.

eligibility.min_work_hours: one route: work in Finland averaging at least 10 hours/week for at least 4 months (aid only for the period you work)
eligibility.income_test: own income affects the amount; for those living with parents, parents' income too
eligibility.residence_requirement: alternatively: EU right of permanent residence, or permanent residence in Finland under the Municipality of Residence Act for a reason other than studies
other: Alternatively: a family member who is an EU/EEA/Swiss (or withdrawal-agreement UK) citizen working in Finland

items.amount: € 279.38/month if living independently; € 43.15-204.42/month living with parents (Kela page, year not stated, read 2026-11-25)
items.how_to_apply: Online in OmaKela (EU citizens without Finnish bank credentials can log in with eIDAS), attaching form OT 10e for foreign residents.
items.stackable: Combined with the student loan guarantee and housing supplement as one 'student financial aid' package; own work income can reduce it.

items.name_it: Borsa di studio statale Kela (opintoraha) - studenti extra-UE
items.description: Non-EU degree students usually cannot get Finnish student financial aid. It is possible only if they came to Finland for a reason other than studies, hold an A, P or P-EU permit (or an EU family-member residence card / withdrawal-agreement card) and live in Finland permanently. A residence permit for studies does not qualify.

eligibility.residence_requirement: permanent residence in Finland under the Municipality of Residence Act, for a reason other than studies
other: Permit types: continuous (A), permanent (P), P-EU, EU family-member residence card or withdrawal-agreement card

items.amount: Same scale as for other recipients (€ 279.38/month living independently, Kela page read 2026-11-25)

items.description: State guarantee for a student loan taken from a bank. Granted automatically to whoever receives a study grant, so the same nationality/residence conditions apply. Kela can later repay part of the loan (student loan compensation) if you graduate on time.

other: Only if you receive the Kela study grant (see fi-study-grant-eu / fi-study-grant-non-eu)

items.amount: up to € 850/month for higher education students studying in Finland (Kela page read 2026-11-25)
items.how_to_apply: Included in the study grant decision; then apply for the loan at a bank.
items.stackable: With the study grant and housing supplement.

items.name_it: Nessun programma statale di borse per bachelor/master
items.authority: Finnish National Agency for Education (EDUFI) - Study in Finland
items.description: Study in Finland states there are no governmental scholarship programmes for bachelor's or master's studies; scholarships and tuition-fee waivers are offered by individual universities, and ads for 'fully funded Finland government scholarships' are misleading. The 'Finland Scholarship' is not mentioned on the official page.
items.how_to_apply: Apply for university scholarships/waivers with the admission application (see university records).
items.notes: The assignment listed a 'Finland Scholarship' to verify: it does not appear on Study in Finland's scholarship pages today, and neither Aalto's nor Helsinki's fee/scholarship page mentions it. Treat it as not currently available unless a university page says otherwise.

items.description: Part of student financial aid: 80% of accepted rent up to a municipal cap, for the months you study. Same nationality/residence conditions as the study grant (EU students usually only via work or permanent residence; non-EU students on a study permit cannot get it). Not available if living with or in a home owned by parents; students living with a child get general housing allowance instead.

eligibility.income_test: partner's and parents' income do not affect the amount
other: Must be eligible for Kela student financial aid (see fi-study-grant-eu / fi-study-grant-non-eu)
Non-EU students with a residence permit for studies cannot get it, nor general housing allowance

items.amount: max € 296/month in Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa, Kauniainen (80% of max accepted rent € 370); € 248 or € 216 elsewhere (Kela page read 2026-11-25, effective date not stated)
items.how_to_apply: OmaKela, with the study grant application.
items.stackable: With study grant and loan guarantee; not with general housing allowance.
items.notes: The assignment hint said students get housing help via general housing allowance; Kela's current page shows a student housing supplement inside student financial aid, with general housing allowance only for specific cases (e.g. living with a child).

items.description: Kela subsidises one meal per day in student restaurants for students based in Finland at a Finnish higher education institution; exchange students at a Finnish institution are eligible too.

other: Must be based in Finland and study at a Finnish higher education institution

items.amount: € 2.80 subsidy per meal; student pays max € 3.10 for a standard meal (Kela page last modified 5 May 2026)
items.how_to_apply: Show a student card at the student restaurant.

items.authority: Kela / Finnish Student Health Service (FSHS / YTHS)
items.description: Degree students registered as attending get general and mental-health care at FSHS for a small fee paid to Kela; EU/EEA/Swiss/UK students with EHIC/GHIC are exempt from the fee and use FSHS by showing the card. Exchange students are not entitled to FSHS.
items.how_to_apply: Pay via OmaKela (no bill sent), or send EHIC image to FSHS and a copy to Kela.
items.deadline: 15 March (spring) / 15 November (autumn) if registered on time

items.name_it: Sconto studenti HSL (trasporti area di Helsinki)
items.description: Discount on HSL season tickets in Helsinki, Espoo, Vantaa and Kauniainen. Degree students need a personal identity code and a DVV municipality of residence; exchange students use a university-stamped HSL application form.

other: Degree students: municipality of residence in the HSL area registered with DVV

items.amount: 40% off season tickets (Aalto); student 30-day ticket about € 50-70/month (Aalto estimate)
items.how_to_apply: HSL app with Finnish strong identification, or HSL travel card at a service point with student card/stamped form.
items.notes: hsl.fi returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches; percentage and price are from Aalto University pages, not the operator.

items.name_it: Esenzione fiscale per studenti da trattati contro la doppia imposizione
items.description: Grants from the home country and EU pocket money are generally not taxed. Some tax treaties exempt part of wages from a Finnish employer when the work is connected to studies pursued in the home country (e.g. € 510/month for stays up to 183 days for Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Hungary, Luxembourg and others; France € 510/month until 31 Dec 2026). Separately, non-residents (stay under 6 months) get a € 510/month deduction before the 35% tax at source.

eligibility.stay_duration: treaty-dependent (often 183 days or less in a calendar year)
other: Depends on the specific tax treaty with your home country; a tax officer checks eligibility when issuing the tax card

items.how_to_apply: Request the tax card at a Tax Administration service point with passport and certificate of study.
items.notes: Whether Italy's treaty includes such an exemption was not visible in the summary read today; do not assume it.

items.name_local: University of Helsinki Scholarship Programme (tuition fee waiver)
items.name_it: Esonero tasse University of Helsinki (50% o 100%)
items.description: Non-EU/EEA students liable for tuition fees (bachelor's € 13,000/year; master's € 13,000, 15,000 or 18,000/year) can apply for a tuition fee waiver in the master's application: mostly 50%, very few 100%. UH English-taught bachelor's graduates finishing on time get 100% (GPA ≥ 3.8/5) or 50% (3.4-3.7). Waivers do not cover living costs. A € 1,000 Dean's award exists for 2nd/3rd-year bachelor's students.

other: Liable for tuition fees (no P permit, EU Blue Card, Brexit permit etc.)
Keep it: at least 55 ECTS per year, full-time study

items.amount: 50% or 100% of the tuition fee, for 2 years (master's)
items.how_to_apply: Same form as the master's application, during the admission period.
items.notes: The page read today describes waivers for master's applicants; it did not state waiver terms for first-year bachelor's applicants.

items.description: Merit-based 100% tuition fee waiver for non-EU/EEA students in English-taught programmes (fees from 1 Aug 2025: bachelor's € 12,000-15,000/year, master's € 15,000-20,000/year). Very limited numbers. Also: 25% discount on the first-year bachelor's fee if paid within 21 days of the acceptance letter, and 25% partner scholarships for some nationalities.

other: Top applicants by programme criteria; waiting-list admits excluded
Keep it: full-time study per personal study plan, for the normative 3 (bachelor's) or 2 (master's) years

items.amount: 100% of the tuition fee (does not cover living costs)
items.how_to_apply: Tick the scholarship option on the admission application; cannot be applied for later. Decision comes with admission and cannot be appealed.
items.stackable: Not with the Pekka Mattila Excellence Scholarship.
